newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria conservatives threaten to outlaw CA sale.
newsitem.headline: Austria conservatives threaten to outlaw CA sale.

text.p: The People's Party, junior partner in Austria's coalition government, said on Wednesday it was sponsoring a bill to annul a future sale of privatisation candidate Creditanstalt to Bank Austria .
"We aim to ensure through an amendment (to the Creditanstalt privatisation law) that this is a genuine privatisation," the People's Party motion said.

The rightist People's Party has slammed "socialist" Bank Austria's bid for Creditanstalt, a conservative stronghold, and urged the finance ministry to reject the offer because Bank Austria is effectively controlled by the City of Vienna.

"The stake must not be sold to public bodies, especially not regional public bodies, nor to companies run by regional public bodies, companies in which regional public bodies are directly or indirectly involved nor public funds, whose losses are covered by a regional public body," the motion said.
People's Party whip Andreas Khol needs the backing of a third of MPs to force a parliamentary vote.
Parliament's next regular session will be at the end of January but the law, if passed, will be retroactive to December 1, effectively making a sale to Bank Austria illegal.
Khol has also threatened to force an emergency session of parliament at the beginning of January.

Bank Austria is one of three bidders chasing the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares. It has reportedly outbid its rivals, an EA-Generali group favoured by the People's Party and entrepreneur Karl Wlaschek.
Social Democrat Finance Minister Viktor Klima has promised a decision by year-end.
